title: Which block will sink?
explanation: The solid block labeled 1.3 g/cm³ is denser than water and sinks; the other blocks are less dense than water.
followup: What would change if the liquid had a density of 1.4 g/cm³?

title: Which ball stores the most gravitational energy?
explanation: With mass and gravity held constant, gravitational potential energy increases with height. B is highest at 4 m.
followup: How could a lower ball store more energy than B?

title: Which way will the canoe move?
explanation: The paddle pushes water backward; the water simultaneously pushes the paddle and canoe forward. These interaction forces act on different objects.
followup: Identify the two objects that exert the interaction forces.

title: Which rock formed from cooling lava?
explanation: Basalt is an igneous rock that can form when lava cools at Earth's surface. Sandstone and shale are sedimentary; marble is metamorphic.
followup: What process could change sandstone into a metamorphic rock?

title: Which pair shows mutualism?
explanation: In this example, the bee obtains food and the flower receives pollination. The other scenes represent parasitism, predation, and a typical commensalism example.
followup: Explain how mutualism differs from commensalism.

title: Which sugar sample dissolves fastest?
explanation: For sugar under these conditions, warmer water, smaller pieces, and stirring each increase the rate of dissolving. D combines all three.
followup: Design a fair test of temperature alone.

title: Which rover has the greatest average speed?
explanation: A averages 5 m/s, B 4 m/s, C 9 m/s, and D 6 m/s. C has the greatest average speed.
followup: How far would C travel in 5 seconds at that average speed?

title: Which handle warms fastest by conduction?
explanation: Among these materials, copper conducts thermal energy most readily, so its handle warms fastest when size and conditions are matched.
followup: Which material would you choose for a handle meant to stay cooler?

title: Which change helps protect the stream?
explanation: A vegetated buffer can slow runoff, trap sediment, and take up some nutrients before they reach the stream.
followup: What evidence would show whether the buffer is helping?

title: Which example shows artificial selection?
explanation: The gardener chooses which plants reproduce based on a desired heritable trait. Human choice drives artificial selection.
followup: Why must the selected trait be heritable for this process to work?

title: What will the scale read after the reaction?
explanation: The whole closed system remains 150 g. Gas formation and atom rearrangement do not change its total mass when nothing enters or leaves.
followup: What could make the measured mass decrease in an open version of this setup?

title: Which cart has the greatest acceleration?
explanation: The accelerations are A 2 m/s², B 1 m/s², C 4 m/s², and D 2 m/s². C has the greatest net force per unit mass.
followup: How would doubling C's mass change its acceleration at the same net force?

title: Which wave can help reveal a bone fracture?
explanation: X-rays penetrate soft tissue more readily than bone, creating contrast that can help reveal a fracture on a radiograph.
followup: Name a different application of electromagnetic waves.

title: Which setting best supports a hurricane?
explanation: Warm ocean water supplies energy and moisture; moist air and weak wind shear help an organized tropical cyclone develop when other necessary conditions are present.
followup: Why can strong wind shear disrupt a developing storm?
choices: Cool water · Dry air · Strong wind shear
Warm water · Moist air · Weak wind shear
Warm water · Dry air · Strong wind shear
Cool water · Moist air · Weak wind shear

title: Where would primary succession begin?
explanation: Primary succession starts on a surface without developed soil, such as newly cooled lava. The other scenes retain soil and represent recovery or ongoing disturbance.
followup: How would soil remaining after a fire affect recovery?
